'''Wang Buxuan''' (5 February 1922 – 31 August 2019), also known as '''Bu-Xuan Wang''' and '''Pu-Hsuan Wang''',<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Peng|first1=XF|last2=Guo|first2=ZY|last3=Hartnett|first3=JP|last4=Minkowycz|first4=WJ|date=March 2002|title=Professor Bu-Xuan Wang, Chinese academician, on his 80th birthday|journal=International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer|volume=45|issue=7|pages=1377–1378|doi=10.1016/s0017-9310(01)00259-9|issn=0017-9310}}</ref> was a Chinese thermal physicist and engineer, considered a pioneer in the field of engineering [[thermodynamics]] in China. He established the engineering thermodynamics program at [[Tsinghua University]] in 1957 and the China Solar Power Society in 1979. He was elected an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1980.

== Early life and education ==
Wang was born 5 February 1922 in [[Wuxi]], [[Jiangsu]], Republic of China. He earned a B.S. from the [[National Southwestern Associated University]] in 1943 and an M.S. in [[mechanical engineering]] from [[Purdue University]] in the United States in 1949.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_4306341|title=工程热物理学科的开拓者、中国科学院院士王补宣逝世|last=Deng Hui 邓晖|date=31 August 2019|website=The Paper|access-date=31 August 2019}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.mmcs.org.cn/gz/1224/2586/2016-03/133802.shtml|title=Wang Buxuan|date=5 March 2016|website=National Museum for Modern Chinese Scientists|access-date=31 August 2019}}</ref>

== Career ==
When the [[People's Republic of China]] was established in 1949, Wang gave up his doctoral studies and returned to China.<ref name=":4" /> He taught at [[Peking University]] before moving to [[Tsinghua University]], where he established the engineering [[thermodynamics]] program in 1957.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.hlhl.org.cn/english/showsub.asp?id=300|title=Wang Buxuan|website=Ho Leung Ho Lee Foundation|access-date=31 August 2019}}</ref> Answering a national need, Wang spent 1963 to 1966 researching the synthesis of [[ammonia]] at a major chemical plant in [[Sichuan]] province. By redesigning a compact heat exchange system to enhance heat transfer and improve catalystic reaction, he doubled the daily production of the plant.<ref name=":3" /> It was listed by the Chinese government as one of the country's 100 important achievements in 1966.<ref name=":3" /> In 1979, Wang founded the China Solar Power Society, and was its chairman until 1987.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.cnste.org/html/jiaodian/2018/0202/2580.html|title=清华大学王补宣院士获中国太阳能科学与技术终身成就奖|date=2 February 2018|website=China Solar Thermal Alliance|access-date=31 August 2019}}</ref>

Wang's research interests were [[heat transfer]], including biomedical heat transfer and heat transfer through porous media, thermal properties of matter, and [[solar energy]]. From 1981 to 1987, he conducted basic research on the "film boiling of subcooled liquid flowing with higher velocity along a solid surface" and  the "evaporation of liquid drops on solid surface", which won the [[State Natural Science Award]] in 1989.<ref name=":3" /> He published more than 400 research papers with more than 2000 [[Science Citation Index|SCI]] citations, and ten monographs or textbooks.<ref name=":4" />

Wang was elected an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1980.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chinavitae.com/biography/Wang_Buxuan/full|title=Biography of Wang Buxuan|website=China Vitae|access-date=31 August 2019}}</ref> He was conferred the Research Scholarship Award of the [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]] in 1985, the Energy for Mankind Prize of the Global Energy Society in 1986, the [[Ho Leung Ho Lee Prize]] for Technological Sciences in 1998,<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> and the Lifetime Achievement Award by the China Solar Thermal Alliance in 2018.<ref name=":2" />

== Personal life and death ==
Wang's eldest son, Wang Ruji (王如骥), is a chemist who served as vice chair of the chemistry department of Tsinghua University.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=http://www.mmcs.org.cn/gz/1224/2589/2016-03/133807.shtml|title="热力"不减的九旬老党员|date=25 March 2016|website=National Museum for Modern Chinese Scientists|access-date=1 September 2019|archive-date=31 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190831232117/http://www.mmcs.org.cn/gz/1224/2589/2016-03/133807.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Wang died on 31 August 2019 in Beijing, aged 97.<ref name=":0" />
